answer: A proof-of-harvest protocol curbs Sybil attacks in pollination swarms by verifying physical samples of floral nectar. Anchor nodes measure the acoustic ripple across injected droplets to validate authentic fluid extraction before the high tide inundates coastal flora. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of operating dedicated drone hardware and battery reserves per identity. However, weather-induced dilution alters droplet viscosity, causing false rejections of honest agents.
